finding.claim: The purge handler calls checkPerm(u, "admin") but discards the boolean result, so the admin check does nothing. Any authenticated user can run purgeAll(). The sibling handler rotateKeys uses mustPerm and returns on failure.
finding.source: Any authenticated low-privilege user sending a request to the purge route. The user comes from the request context via userFrom(r) at handlers.go:25.
finding.sink: purgeAll() at handlers.go:27, a destructive admin-only operation.

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) loads the caller's user from the request context
checkPerm(u, "admin") returns a bool that is not used and not branched on, so there is no abort and no 403
Comparison: rotateKeys uses mustPerm and returns when it fails, which is the correct pattern

finding.guards_checked: checkPerm (handlers.go:12-14) only returns the permission bool and never writes a response or aborts. Its result is discarded at line 26, so it is not enforced. No other check exists in the handler. I could not read any route registration or middleware because only handlers.go exists in the directory. The finding rests on the handler itself having no enforced admin check.

verdict.guard_found: checkPerm (handlers.go:12-14) returns a bool only and never aborts; its result is discarded at line 26. No other check in the handler. Route registration and middleware are not in the directory, so an upstream admin-only middleware can't be ruled out.
verdict.reason: handlers.go:26 calls checkPerm(u, "admin") as a bare statement with the result discarded, so purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any authenticated user, unlike rotateKeys at handlers.go:33, which returns when mustPerm fails.
